title: How many dimensions is the alpha rhythm? SVD entropy (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against antropy

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples); spatial map uses all 64 channels
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: SVD entropy (Roberts 1999) measures a signal's dimensionality: time-delay embed it and read the Shannon entropy of the embedding matrix's normalized singular-value spectrum -- low for a structured (e.g. oscillatory) signal, high for a complex one. The ecosystem's complexity suite (permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Hjorth, sample/approximate entropy, DFA, RQA) lacked this singular-value view; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, svdEntropy. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel it reproduces antropy.svd_entropy BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16; both via LAPACK SVD), and the finding: SVD entropy is lower over the posterior alpha region (all 9 posterior channels below the frontal mean) -- the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is a comparatively low-dimensional oscillation.

claims.statement: SVD entropy of the posterior channel POz, in bits -- the signal's dimensionality index
max |svdEntropy - antropy.svd_entropy| (bit-exact; both via LAPACK SVD)
samples in the analyzed channel (10 s at 160 Hz)
mean SVD entropy over the posterior (parieto-occipital) channels
mean SVD entropy over the frontal channels -- higher (more high-dimensional)
posterior channels (of 9) with SVD entropy below the frontal mean -- robustness of the low-dimensional-posterior finding

validation.reference: The newly-authored svdEntropy op is validated against antropy.svd_entropy. antropy re-computes the SVD entropy from the same signal (matched embedding order 3, delay 1). The agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16) because R's svd() and numpy's np.linalg.svd both call LAPACK, so the singular values -- and hence the normalized-spectrum Shannon entropy -- match to the floating-point floor. The finding: SVD entropy is lower over the posterior alpha region (all 9 posterior channels below the frontal mean; posterior 1.239 vs frontal 1.287).
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz for the certified op; all 64 channels for the spatial map
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored svdEntropy reproduces antropy.svd_entropy bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~2e-16); (2) SVD entropy is lower over the posterior alpha region (9/9 posterior channels below the frontal mean). HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a gap -- the ecosystem's complexity suite (permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Hjorth, sample/approximate entropy, DFA, RQA) lacked the singular-value-spectrum complexity view; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- svdEntropy and antropy compute the IDENTICAL SVD-entropy via LAPACK SVD, so the ~2e-16 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) the finding -- lower SVD entropy posteriorly -- indicates the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is a comparatively low-dimensional oscillation, consistent with the Welch/spectrogram/Hjorth/coherence cases on the SAME data; a descriptive spatial pattern on one subject/segment, not a clinical claim; the absolute value depends on the embedding (order 3, delay 1); (4) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: SVD entropy depends on the embedding (order, delay); a sweep over order/delay -- and a contrast of eyes-closed vs eyes-open (alpha present vs suppressed) -- would show whether the posterior low-dimensionality tracks the alpha rhythm specifically. Documented, not escalated.
